missionPremise: `packages/adapters/src/hydrology/noaaAtlas14.ts` `parsePfdsDepthTable` parses a `<tr><td>` HTML table, but the live HDSC endpoint returns a JavaScript array-literal payload (`quantiles=[[...]]`), so the parser never matches and the no-parameter path falls through to Bastrop's 9.5 in regional default under a NOAA citation. CONFIRMED both halves first-hand by curl of the live endpoint and by direct read of the parser and of every caller: the live endpoint returned `result = 'values';` + a `quantiles` array literal at 2026-09-18T22:28:56Z (HTTP 200, 5074 bytes), and the parser's only matching rule was `<tr><td><tr><td>` extraction. Exactly one caller existed (fetchNoaaAtlas14PointEstimate), so there was no second reader of the raw payload.

Knowledge that a raw-body hash is not a stable identity for hdsc.nws.noaa.gov because of `pyRunTime`; anything keying on a raw hash of that endpoint will flake.

LESSON: A fixture written by hand to match the code's assumption proves only that the code matches the fixture. The `<tr><td>` table here was never served by the endpoint; it kept the suite green for the entire life of the defect. The test of a fixture is a hash of a payload captured live at a stated moment, not its resemblance to the parser.

A default that is presented under a source citation is worse than an absence: an absence forces a decision, a mis-cited default is silently believed. The cheap-looking literal `?? 4` was the more dangerous half of this defect than the parser miss, because it also made the route classify the run as FULL coverage (designStormCount 0 -> not degraded).

Two points matter more than one in a location-dependent measurement. Both the parser and the route returned a single number for a >400-mile span before the fix, and one point alone would have shown a plausible number rather than a constant.

A whitespace-only reformat is the cheapest divergence control for a refusal: it must still parse. Without it, 'refuses garbage' cannot be separated from 'refuses everything', and a parser that refuses everything would have passed 12/12.
Map gitattributes the fixture extension before writing the fixture. LF vs CRLF changed the bytes and would have changed the hash that the close cites.
DEAD-END: Comparing a raw-body sha256 of hdsc.nws.noaa.gov to a fixture: the payload embeds `pyRunTime = <float>`, so two consecutive fetches of identical data differ (measured 5073 vs 5074 bytes). Everything keys on quantilesLiteralSha256 instead. Do not re-introduce a raw-body hash as an identity.

Cross-validating the matrix's axis meaning from the unlabeled payload alone: the quantiles matrix has no row labels. Labeled semantics came from `fe_text.csv` at the same endpoint, which is the only reason the row/column indices are defensible. Do not derive axis meaning from row order alone.
